candidates.title: Map variable invoice rows into a request

demandEvidence.chore: Map variable CRM invoice-row data into an external system request.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: I cannot map array data for dynamic amount of invoice rows to the HTTP POST module’s “invoice rows” section.

ease.reason: A sample array can be mapped by hand; Make docs explain indexed array mapping, but not this external invoice API.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: automation consultants may pay for repeatable invoice mapping help; no buyer or payment is shown.

feasibility.reason: A four-week synthetic test can transform sample rows, but the endpoint contract and successful persistence are unknown.

autonomy.reason: A transform could repeat, but the supplied docs cover array mapping only; a person must validate totals and authorize sending.

evidence.reason: The post gives the mapping problem and sample arrays; docs support array indexing, not Make execution, invoice persistence, or tax correctness.

candidates.reason: The literal mapping chore supports a narrow synthetic payload experiment. The mean is 4.6, below threshold; documentation supports array mapping only, not execution or correct invoice creation.

experimentPlan.output: A reviewable JSON request body with one output row per supplied invoice row.
experimentPlan.trigger: An operator pastes a sample row array and expected body shape.
steps: Parse each supplied row array.
Map each row to operator-defined output fields.
Show the proposed JSON body without sending it.
Compare row count and selected values with the input.
Flag missing or mismatched fields for review.
experimentPlan.acceptanceCheck: For a fixed synthetic input, confirm output row count and selected values match the operator-provided expected body.
experimentPlan.humanBoundary: The operator defines the external schema, checks amounts and tax fields, and authorizes any real request; production access and persistence are not tested.
unverified: No reference establishes Make scenario execution.
The external endpoint schema and response are unknown.
Invoice persistence and tax correctness are unverified.

candidates.title: Summarize long email threads for review

demandEvidence.chore: Create a compact, linked summary of each new email within a long conversation.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: every single new email is resume like : “X person ask X person if there is a possibility to do X in comparaison of original X”

ease.reason: A student can test summaries with fictional threads, but no supplied implementation reference supports email access or stable message IDs.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: professional service firms handling long email threads may pay for compact context; the post gives no buyer evidence.

feasibility.reason: A four-week test can summarize sample threads and preserve source-message labels; live mailbox access and reliable identity remain unknown.

autonomy.reason: A proposed summarize-and-link cycle can repeat, but a person must confirm references and review sensitive or ambiguous content.

evidence.reason: The post describes compacting long email conversations and immutable-ID concerns; frequency and demand beyond this post are unknown.

candidates.reason: The task/context span supports a bounded fictional-thread summary experiment. No supplied implementation reference is available; the mean is 4.6, below threshold.

experimentPlan.output: A compact thread summary with each statement linked to a supplied message ID.
experimentPlan.trigger: An operator submits a fictional thread for summarization.
steps: Separate messages using supplied labels.
Draft a short summary of the request and latest status.
Attach the supplied label to each summary point.
Compare extracted points with the original sample.
Flag uncertain or conflicting statements for human review.
experimentPlan.acceptanceCheck: Check that each summary point matches the cited sample message and that no unsupported detail appears.
experimentPlan.humanBoundary: The operator supplies test data and reviews every summary; no live mailbox access, stable Microsoft ID integration, or real email processing is established.
unverified: Email access and immutable ID handling are unsupported.
Summary accuracy on real threads is unknown.
A single discussion does not establish recurring buyer demand.

candidates.title: Compare AWS scaling options from supplied costs

demandEvidence.chore: Assess affordable AWS scaling options for a bootstrapped startup.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: need to scale on AWS but can't afford it

ease.reason: A student could format operator-supplied cost scenarios, but no reference supports AWS cost analysis.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: bootstrapped startups may pay for affordable scaling advice; the post offers help but establishes no buyer payment.

feasibility.reason: A four-week mock can compare a few supplied scenarios, while current AWS pricing and workload fit remain unverified.

autonomy.reason: A draft comparison can be generated from supplied inputs, but a qualified person must verify prices and approve infrastructure choices.

evidence.reason: The post asks for help scaling AWS affordably but includes no concrete cost fields, analysis method, or corroboration.

candidates.reason: A narrow cost-options memo can be proposed from operator-supplied data, but the source gives no actual costs or analysis method; the mean is 3.8.

experimentPlan.output: A short comparison memo showing operator-supplied infrastructure scenarios and unresolved cost questions.
experimentPlan.trigger: An operator provides sample costs and a workload description.
steps: List the supplied options and their stated costs.
Compare each option with the supplied budget.
Summarize trade-offs using only provided details.
Mark missing price or workload assumptions.
Ask a human reviewer to verify all figures and conclusions.
experimentPlan.acceptanceCheck: Confirm each cost and workload statement traces to an input and that unknown prices are clearly marked.
experimentPlan.humanBoundary: A person supplies and verifies current prices and approves any infrastructure change; no AWS retrieval, optimization, or deployment is supported.
unverified: No implementation reference supports AWS cost analysis.
Current pricing and workload requirements are unverified.
The source does not establish recurring demand.

candidates.title: Draft order status updates when data is unclear

demandEvidence.chore: Prepare customer-facing order-status updates when internal order data changes or is incomplete.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: I’d be interested to hear how others handle customer-facing status updates when internal operational data is incomplete or changes frequently.

ease.reason: Synthetic order examples can test a draft-and-hold flow; source describes a Make-based debounce mechanism but not a reusable supported build capability.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: online shops may pay for clearer order updates; this discussion establishes a stated need, not payment.

feasibility.reason: A four-week sample can draft updates and suppress stale events, but live ClickUp or store access and correctness remain unverified.

autonomy.reason: A proposed event-to-draft loop can repeat; the source describes debounce and not guessing missing data, while a person must resolve gaps and approve messages.

evidence.reason: The post asks about customer-facing status messages with incomplete or changing operations data and describes debounce; broader demand is unverified.

candidates.reason: The retained task span supports a scoped draft-and-hold experiment, but the post is primarily a maker explanation and request for discussion; the mean is 4.6.

experimentPlan.output: A draft order-status message that pauses when required status fields are missing or stale.
experimentPlan.trigger: An operator supplies a test order update or a newer replacement event.
steps: Compare event timestamps for the same test order.
Ignore a stale event when a newer one is supplied.
Draft a message only from complete approved fields.
Hold the draft when fields are missing or unclear.
Ask a person to approve any customer message.
experimentPlan.acceptanceCheck: Use a fixed synthetic event sequence to confirm only the newest complete status is drafted and missing data produces a hold.
experimentPlan.humanBoundary: The operator defines fields, rules, and test data and approves every message; live integrations, delivery, and customer outcomes are not tested.
unverified: No reference establishes a deployable Make implementation.
The behavior on real store and operations data is unknown.
A single post does not establish buyer or payment evidence.

steps.message: Assessed all eight assigned discussion identities. Four concrete chores received bounded proposed experiments and five provisional ratings; each mean is below six. Four vague, product-only, or one-off items were excluded with evidence-based reasons. No post proposed.
